title: Волшебник Макс и проверка Нагиева  (Max the Magician and Nagiyev's Check-In)

segments.t: Max carries a freshly prepared dish out to the dining room for his older admirer, who praises its aroma and calls him a true magician. Meanwhile, Dmitriy Nagiyev greets Vika at the bar and is relieved to hear that everything in the restaurant is running smoothly.
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
'Here you go, please enjoy.' The meaning hinges on 'there you go' working together with 'there you go' in spoken Russian.
'Oh my, Max, you have outdone yourself again.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'come on' and finishing on 'again'. Vika answers right away.
'Do not worry at all, it is my pleasure.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'not' before landing on 'pleasant'.
'Do you mind if I sit?' Max brings out the contrast between 'you' and 'not' in a few short words.
'No, no, I do not mind at all.' The negative particle sits right before the verb meaning 'there is no' to negate the statement. Vika answers right away.
'What a wonderful aroma.' The grammar packs 'what' and 'aroma' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'You are a magician, Max.' Max brings out the contrast between 'you' and 'a wizard' in a few short words.
'I did my very best, specially for you.' Notice the reflexive suffix on the verb meaning 'tried', turning the action back on the subject. Vika answers right away.
'Hello there, Viktoriya Sergeyevna.' The meaning hinges on 'hello' working together with 'Sergeyevna' in spoken Russian.
'Have a seat, Viktoriya Sergeyevna.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'sit down' before landing on 'Sergeyevna'.
'Everything in the restaurant is going fine.' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'restaurant', while 'fine' completes the thought. Vika answers right away.
'Aha, well thank goodness for that.' In Russian, the idea of 'yeah' flows naturally into 'to God' without extra filler words.
'What are you staring at?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'what' before landing on 'are staring'. Let's hear the complete conversation once more.
